title: hybrid-deadline-scheduler-and-kv-anticipation-to-smooth-streaming-latency
author: Maya Thompson
release_notes: Introduce hybrid deadline-based streaming scheduler + anticipatory KV prefetch and credit-smoothing. Improves median TTFB by ~11% and p95 by up to 28% on typical streaming workloads. Backwards-compatible; feature gated behind runtime flags.
description:
Motivation and summary:
This PR introduces a hybrid deadline-based scheduler combined with an anticipatory KV prefetch heuristic and a credit-smoothing replenishment algorithm to reduce streaming token-generation latency variance. Existing continuous-batching and emit/flush mechanisms reduce cost but still exhibit tail jitter when short-lived interactive streams contend with larger batched workloads. The goal is to smooth first-byte and inter-token latency without regressing throughput or increasing GPU stalls.

Design highlights (single-string description):
1) Hybrid deadline scheduler: requests carry a soft deadline derived from observed end-to-end SLOs and recent prefix latencies. The scheduler blends earliest-deadline-first for latency-sensitive lanes with throughput-oriented coalescing for bulk lanes. A short window (configurable, default 10ms) is reserved to let imminent short streams preempt larger microbatches.
2) Anticipatory KV prefetch: when a request's prefix matches a high-probability prefix (hot-token prefixes maintained by a lightweight LRU+freq estimator), we issue tentative KV prefetches into the local KV cache before kernel launch. Prefetches are conservative (max 2 per request) and cancelable to avoid evicting cold state.
3) Credit-smoothing replenishment: instead of refilling emission credits in large discrete jumps (which lead to microbursts), we use an exponential moving-average (EMA) based replenishment that paces token emission credit growth to steady-state. Combined with the scheduler, this reduces queue oscillation.
4) Fallback and feature gating: the behavior is behind two runtime feature flags (hybrid_deadline=true, kv_anticipation=true). If flags are disabled, system falls back to previous continuous-batching path.

Implementation notes:
- New files: runtime/scheduler/hybrid_deadline_scheduler.go, runtime/scheduler/deadline_policy_test.go, runtime/kv/anticipatory_prefetch.go, runtime/kv/prefetch_metrics.go, runtime/emitter/credit_smoother.go, and small wiring in runtime/service/stream_handler.go.
- The scheduler integrates with the existing batch coordinator: it exposes a scheduling hint API (softDeadline, laneHint) so we avoid deep coupling.
- Prefetch uses the existing KV async loader interface; added a cancel token so prefetched payloads are discarded if not used within 40ms.
- Credit smoother is lock-free for the hot path; uses atomic counters + timer-based lightweight tick on emit loop.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests added for deadline logic, prefetch cancellation, and credit smoothing edge cases.
- Microbench: streaming harness with 100 concurrent interactive connections and a background bulk workload. Observed changes relative to d0 (main): median TTFB -11%, p95 TTFB -28%, token stepping p99 reduced by 40% in tuned configs. Throughput loss: <1% on heavy batch workloads.
- Production canary: rolled out to canary pool (5 machines) for 48h; no increased GPU stall signals in telemetry and no cache thrashing alarms.
